assessment.nobel_worthiness: Foundational theory in two linked areas: the political economy of trade protection (the 'protection for sale' framework) and the integration of endogenous growth with international trade and technology diffusion. Both reshaped how economists model policy formation and the global transmission of ideas. The work has been durable for three decades, with clear influence on later trade, growth and political-economy research.
assessment.attribution: The two-person core is clean and the joint contributions are widely recognised. Helpman has further major contributions (monopolistic competition in trade, firm heterogeneity) that strengthen his case, but the Grossman-Helpman partnership is the natural unit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. The key papers and the books date from the late 1980s to the 1990s, and their ideas are standard in graduate curricula. The prize has not recognised trade theory since 2008, so there is no timing obstacle.
uncertainties: Krugman (2008) already covered new trade theory, so the committee may judge part of the trade-theory space as addressed.
Helpman also appears on another trade candidate (B041), so the committee may favour a different configuration.
Empirical validation of the political-economy trade models is mixed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Created the modern field of political economics, using formal models and empirical tests to study how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes. The work is widely used, and it is a systematic research programme, not a single result.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the most consistently credited pair (Political Economics: Explaining Economic Policy and their constitutional-economics programme). Besley's work on state capacity and accountability is also central. Credit is shared and somewhat diffuse, so a three-person grouping is defensible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with core contributions from the 1990s and 2000s and a large follow-on literature. The 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity (Acemoglu, Johnson, Robinson) is adjacent, so timing needs care.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize may make the committee reluctant to reward a nearby area so soon.
Whether Besley should be in the group or the prize should go to a pair is uncertain.
Possible institutional or personal proximity of some candidates to committee members should be disclosed even though it is not adjudicated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities, forward-looking pricing and rule-based monetary policy is the working paradigm of central banks. Calvo's staggered pricing, Taylor's rule and staggered contracts, and Woodford's synthesis in Interest and Prices are the key building blocks. Policy and academic impact are very large.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across many authors (Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and others). Limiting to three requires a judgement that favours foundational ingredients over estimation and implementation. Calvo, Taylor and Woodford are the best-defined trio, but other trios are arguable.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature. The ideas are decades old, the framework has been tested through the financial crisis and the post-pandemic inflation, and the criticisms are well known.
uncertainties: Choosing three from at least eight plausible contributors may lead to credit disputes.
The 2022-24 inflation episode and heterogeneous-agent critiques have prompted debate about the framework's adequacy.
Prior prizes to Phelps, Lucas, Kydland-Prescott and Bernanke (2022) partly cover adjacent ground.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: 'Credit Cycles' (1997) showed how collateral constraints and asset prices create amplification and persistence in macroeconomic fluctuations. It gave the basis for much of the post-2008 macro-finance literature and for policy analysis of financial frictions. The impact on both theory and policy is deep.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the collateral-constraint mechanism. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the related financial-accelerator line, but Bernanke's 2022 prize partly covered that area, so I restrict the proposal to the cleaner two-person core.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The paper dates from 1997 and has been repeatedly validated and extended after the 2007-09 crisis.
uncertainties: The committee might prefer a broader grouping that includes Gertler, which would shift the attribution.
The 2022 prize (Bernanke, Diamond, Dybvig) covered related financial-crisis themes and may reduce appetite for a near neighbour.
Empirical identification of collateral channels is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reframed the analysis of labour demand by showing how technology and trade reshape tasks, wages and local labour markets. The skill-biased/task-based work and the 'China shock' results changed both research and policy debate on inequality and globalisation. The influence is high and the empirical design is credible.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task approach and the trade-shock work, Hanson to the trade-shock and local-labour-market evidence, and Katz to the long-run race between education and technology. Dorn is an important co-author, and Acemoglu's 2024 prize overlapped on tasks and technology, so the credit boundary is subtle.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature, with the key papers from 1990s to 2013 and a large follow-up literature. Some of the China-shock conclusions are still debated, and long-run effects continue to be assessed.
uncertainties: Overlap with Acemoglu's recognised work on technology and tasks.
Some robustness and interpretation questions remain around the China-shock estimates.
Katz also appears in other candidates (e.g. B002), so the committee may favour different groupings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Constructed long-run historical series on top incomes and wealth from tax data, which put distributional questions back at the centre of economics and public debate. The measurement contribution is major and has been widely adopted by statistical agencies and researchers. Theoretical and policy interpretations are more contested than the data work.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the key originators of the top-incomes methodology (the 2003 QJE paper). Zucman's contributions on wealth and offshore holdings are important but more recent and more contested in measurement.
assessment.maturity: Largely mature on the income-series side. The wealth-distribution measurement debates, including the choice of capitalisation methods and the treatment of offshore wealth, are still active.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes about wealth-concentration estimates and the policy conclusions drawn from them.
Whether the committee regards the contribution as primarily data construction rather than conceptual advance.
The pair-versus-trio question depends on how recent offshore-wealth work is weighed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rubinstein's 1982 alternating-offers bargaining model is the canonical non-cooperative bargaining result and is used throughout economics and political science. The Rubinstein-Wolinsky work on decentralised markets with bargaining links bargaining to search and market outcomes. The contribution is fundamental, though the overall volume of work is narrower than for other candidates.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein is the clear originator. Wolinsky's market-bargaining contribution is a distinct and well-credited extension. Binmore made important related contributions (including the link to Nash bargaining), but the primary credit rests with Rubinstein.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with about forty years of validation and use. Game theory has been recognised before (Nash, Harsanyi, Selten, Aumann, Schelling, Myerson and others), so the timing is fine but the competition is stiff.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees bargaining theory as sufficiently distinct from earlier game-theory prizes.
Binmore's role is arguable and could change the proposed grouping.
Empirical relevance of the alternating-offers model is limited in the lab and field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Foundations of Open-Economy Macroeconomics (1996) and the 'redux' models brought intertemporal optimisation and nominal rigidities into international macro. Their 'exchange-rate disconnect' and 'six major puzzles' papers set the research agenda in the field. The impact on both academic work and policy institutions is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the clear joint originators of the intertemporal open-economy framework, with Obstfeld's contribution especially central to its textbook form. Rogoff's other work (exchange-rate puzzles, central-bank design, crises) adds to his case but overlaps with another ballot.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with three decades of use. The puzzles identified remain only partly resolved, which signals a lasting agenda but also that the central empirical questions are unsettled.
uncertainties: Mundell (1999) and Krugman (2008) have recognised neighbouring international-economics work.
Some key puzzles remain unresolved, so the contribution is partly an agenda rather than a settled result.
Rogoff appears on another candidate (B033), which could split support.
